data.name: Barrow
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English beorg or barrow, meaning 'hill' or 'barrow'. This name may have been given to someone living on a hill or to someone with a shining or bright personality. In the context of Christianity, it could be a reference to the hill where Jesus was crucified or the hill where He ascended into heaven.

data.cultural_impact: The name Barrow has historical ties to the Old English language and may have been associated with the physical landscape of ancient Europe. In 15th-century England, it was a common surname for people who lived near a hill or barrow, an ancient mound of earth or stones. In modern times, the name has spread globally and taken on new meanings and associations.

It can also represent the importance of lifting up one another in prayer and in deed, reaching new heights of faith together.
